page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. In benchmark evaluations, the single-core performance of the Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, and the bottom 10% for single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core execution scales to average performance tiers, as demonstrated by middle-50% results in multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark CPU tests.

Memory performance is stable, with read-only and write bandwidth benchmarks registering in the middle 50% tier. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also align with average performance expectations. For machine learning tasks, LLM inference speeds for text generation using a medium 7B model achieve average throughput, though prompt processing and smaller model text generation fall into the weaker performance brackets.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge offers a balanced option for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage its 24 dedicated cores without requiring high per-core performance or massive memory footprints. It is suitable for workloads such as multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and parallel batch processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 48.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lacks local storage, relying on network-attached storage. While single-core benchmarks for this hardware generation are weak, multi-core performance scales to average levels across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests. Memory bandwidth, Redis operations, and static web serving throughput also perform in the average tier. The instance is best suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, and parallel batch processing where dedicated CPU allocation is required but extreme single-thread speed is not critical.
